newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan, Philippines sign nuclear energy accord.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan, Philippines sign nuclear energy accord.

text.p: Pakistan and the Philippines signed an agreement on the use of nuclear energy on Saturday after talks between visiting President Fidel Ramos and Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif.

Ramos later told a news conference that the accord, signed by Pakistan's Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan and Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon would cover fields such as power generation, agriculture, industry, medicine, sanitation and hydrology.
It will be implemented by Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission and the Philippine Nuclear Research Institute, he said.

Ramos said the two sides had also agreed "to take steps to expand our ties in trade, investment, energy, including nuclear energy, agriculture, industry, human resources development and defence cooperation".

Pakistan says it can make nuclear weapons but has decided not to do so, maintaining its nuclear programme is for peaceful purposes only. Western governments believe Pakistan, like its arch-rival India, could quickly assemble nuclear weapons.
Ramos, who arrived in Friday for a three-day visit, said the Pakistani and Philippine foreign ministers also signed a memorandum of understanding to hold annual bilateral policy consultations.
Earlier in their talks, Ramos and Sharif agreed to set up a Business Council that will explore ways to boost their commercial ties, the official APP news agency said.
Ramos said his country would back Pakistan's bid to become a full dialogue partner in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

APP said Ramos asked Sharif during the talks to send a business delegation to Manila to seek ways to promote trade between the two countries, and official sources said the delegation was expected to visit Manila shortly.

Sharif briefed Ramos on the current situation in the Indian-ruled part of the disputed Hiamalayan region of Kashmir, on neighbouring Afghanistan and the forthcoming foreign secretary level talks between India and Pakistan, it said.
The two leaders also discussed the signing of extradition treaties between the two countries and measures to combat drug trafficking, money laundering and corruption.
Ramos told the news conference the extradition treaty would be discussed further by the interior ministers of the two countries.
Ramos is the first head of state to visit Pakistan since Sharif became prime minister last month.
